subject: Virtual coffee? - annotation efficiency
text:
Hi [NAME],

I met Max Curie from IAS's data science team at ICCV - sounds like human
annotation and taxonomy work are central for brand safety and contextual
relevance. Given your close involvement with both teams at IAS, I wanted to
reach out for a chat.

From our projects with other content verification teams (DoubleVerify &
Zefr) - frame-by-frame, manual annotation is a typical bottleneck. Encord
helps orchestrate AI-automated classification and human review in one
place, so your team can focus on evaluating edge cases and iterating
labelling guidelines with minimal handoffs to data science teams.

How are you thinking about annotation efficiency at IAS? I'm flexible Wed -
Fri this week.

subject: Darwin - chat
text:
Hey [NAME],

Understand you're currently a V7 customer - we've recently had a number of
teams migrate to Encord as V7 has shifted focus away from Darwin, and
several mentioned challenges with labelling service quality - is this
something you've also run into?

We work with teams like Zeitview, Zipline, and Skydio who rely heavily on
high-volume video. We're built to be video-native, support multimodal
workflows, and we just launched SAM3-powered pre-labeling to speed up
annotation. We also provide consistent & reliable annotation services.

Would you be open to a quick 15 mins call early next week for us to chat?

subject: Finetuning Parsing/Extraction
text:

I was curious if your team has been doing this and if so if you'd be open
to a quick conversation?

subject: Data Platform for Perception Teams
text:
Hi [NAME],

We've been working with perception teams at Boston Dynamics, Toyota Woven
and 1X Robotics on multimodal ML workflows.

Encord's data engine lets teams work directly with 3D point clouds, LiDAR,
radar, and multi-sensor data alongside video in a single pipeline.

Teams are using it to build crisp, high-fidelity annotations and to unify
what would otherwise be siloed 2D, 3D, and sensor workflows.

Is this something that would be relevant for your work? If not, is there a
team at [COMPANY] who owns multimodal perception data that might benefit
from a unified platform?

subject: Data Layer for Labeling w/ Deep Mind
text:
Hey [NAME],

One pattern we're seeing with our customers like 1X Robotics and Boston
Dynamics is that even with frontier VLA models, you still need a strong
robot-specific data engine.

Encord helps humanoid teams turn teleop demos and multi-camera/depth
sequences into clean, versioned datasets for training and regression
testing.

It's how they mine edge cases, keep manipulation/locomotion evaluation
consistent, and tighten the perception→action loop as hardware evolves.

I'd invite you to check out [LINK] and let me know what you think.
